articles.title: Educação do futuro: o que as escolas estão ensinando além do conteúdo | G1
articles.standfirst: STEAM, robótica e inglês ganham espaço na formação; Escola SESI Goiás reúne essas experiências e abre matrículas para 2027
articles.summary: STEAM, robótica e inglês ganham espaço na formação; Escola SESI Goiás reúne essas experiências e abre matrículas para 2027
articles.body:
Com a metodologia STEAM, ensino maker e robótica, os alunos são incentivados a criar e solucionar desafios — Foto: Magnific/IA

A escola que uma criança começa hoje pode ser bem diferente daquela que seus pais frequentaram. Afinal, a inteligência artificial já faz parte da rotina dos estudantes, novas profissões surgem enquanto outras se transformam e habilidades antes associadas principalmente ao mercado de trabalho começam a ser desenvolvidas ainda na educação básica. Os números ajudam a dimensionar esse cenário. Dados do Programa Internacional de Avaliação de Estudantes (PISA) 2025 mostram que 48% dos estudantes brasileiros de 15 anos usam chatbots de inteligência artificial para ajudá-los a aprender pelo menos uma vez por semana. Ao mesmo tempo, na avaliação de resolução de problemas com ferramentas computacionais, os brasileiros obtiveram média de 406 pontos, abaixo da média de 500 pontos registrada pelos países da Organização para a Cooperação e Desenvolvimento Econômico (OCDE).

O desafio, então, não está apenas em colocar a tecnologia dentro da escola, mas em preparar o estudante para compreender, questionar e utilizar essas ferramentas. É nesse contexto que propostas que aproximam conhecimento e prática ganham espaço. Na Escola SESI Goiás, a formação inclui experiências com STEAM, cultura maker e robótica, além da preparação para o Enem e da certificação em inglês TOEFL. A proposta é tratar a tecnologia não como um fim em si mesma, mas como uma ferramenta de aprendizagem.

Imagine uma atividade em que a resposta não está no final da página do livro. O aluno precisa descobrir como chegar até ela. Pode ser construindo um protótipo, programando um robô, testando uma hipótese ou buscando uma solução para um problema. Se não funcionar, é preciso entender o erro, fazer ajustes e tentar novamente. Essa é uma das lógicas por trás da metodologia STEAM, que integra ciência, tecnologia, engenharia, artes e matemática em projetos e situações práticas. Na cultura maker, essa lógica se traduz em atividades nas quais criar, testar, modificar e experimentar passam a fazer parte do processo de aprendizagem.

A proposta também dialoga com o interesse dos próprios estudantes pela descoberta. No PISA 2025, 76,5% dos jovens brasileiros disseram gostar de aprender coisas novas na escola, enquanto 76,2% afirmaram gostar de entender como as coisas funcionam. Na Escola SESI Goiás, esse aprendizado prático aparece em diferentes etapas da formação. Nas atividades de robótica, por exemplo, os estudantes desenvolvem projetos que envolvem programação, construção e resolução de problemas.

A metodologia STEAM utilizada pela rede também inclui experiências com prototipagem, impressão 3D e modelagem computacional. Mais do que aprender a operar uma ferramenta, a proposta é colocar o estudante diante de situações em que ele precisa pensar sobre o que está fazendo e encontrar caminhos para chegar a uma solução.

E quando chega a hora de escolher um caminho?

Por mais que a escola prepare para o futuro, chega um momento em que ele deixa de ser uma ideia distante. No ensino médio, o estudante começa a pensar no Enem, na universidade, em uma profissão e, para alguns, em possibilidades de estudar ou trabalhar fora do país. Por isso, a formação acadêmica continua sendo essencial. No Brasil, a escolaridade também influencia as oportunidades profissionais. Segundo a OCDE, adultos brasileiros de 25 a 64 anos com formação superior ganham, em média, 148% mais do que aqueles que concluíram apenas o ensino médio.

O domínio de outros idiomas também pode ampliar possibilidades. É nesse ponto que entra a certificação TOEFL, oferecida aos estudantes do ensino médio da Escola SESI Goiás. Reconhecido internacionalmente, o exame comprova o nível de proficiência em inglês e pode ser utilizado em processos acadêmicos e oportunidades que exigem conhecimento formal do idioma. A preparação para o Enem, aliada à certificação em inglês, amplia as possibilidades dos estudantes tanto no Brasil quanto no exterior.

Mas a verdade é que ninguém sabe exatamente quais serão as profissões mais procuradas no futuro. Uma criança que hoje está na educação infantil ainda levará muitos anos para chegar ao mercado de trabalho.

Por isso, preparar para o futuro não significa tentar antecipar todas as respostas. A escola pode, no entanto, ampliar as ferramentas que o estudante terá para lidar com as mudanças: contato com tecnologia, estímulo à curiosidade, capacidade de trabalhar em equipe, autonomia para buscar soluções e uma base acadêmica consistente.

Na Escola SESI Goiás, a proposta reúne essas diferentes frentes da educação infantil ao ensino médio. A formação combina conteúdos acadêmicos com STEAM, cultura maker, robótica, preparação para o Enem e inglês com certificação TOEFL. Para as famílias que já estão planejando o próximo ano letivo, as matrículas para 2027 estão abertas. Informações sobre a escola e o processo de matrícula estão disponíveis em sesigoias.com.br/matriculas2027 ou pelo telefone (62) 4002-6213.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Pop-Up: The DMZ Has Never Been This Much Fun
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Pop-Up: The DMZ Has Never Been This Much Fun
articles.body:
Having just returned to Oz from a review trip at Infinity Ward, I was in a pretty good position to judge how authentic (and fun) a Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Pop-Up Experience could be. As luck would have it, Sydney recently hosted just such a shenanigan for press, content creators, lucky Xbox Fan Fest attendees and there were some limited slots open to the public via registrations. I infiltrated it fully.

Let me bust out my Tac-map and give you a sitrep on how the organisers decided to… well, run DMZ (as in a recreation of a real Korean demilitarised zone). The result was a limited-time, MW4-themed mini-extravaganza built around a series of virtual and physical challenges. In next to no time, my objectives list was overflowing with around a dozen POIs to visit across the Carriageworks event space.

Think interactive games, hands-on MW4 Campaign gameplay, photo opps and prizes for the exceptionally skilled.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Pop-Up Activation Sydney

To be honest, I wasn’t sure if I would be among the exceptionally skilled. Working in my favour: I was one of only a handful of folks who’d already finished MW4 (and on its unlockable Realism difficulty, no less). Working against that massive headstart: 15 hours of jetlag and severe sleep deprivation.

It was a 50/50, comrades. I’d blitz this event or pass out midway.

When about sixty of us were marched into the event, I was mighty impressed with the dank, smoke-machine-assisted scene that greeted me. The organisers had nailed the DMZ duality aesthetic of two vastly different Koreas fighting over the one peninsula. Entry required picking a side, North or South, and a razor wire fence bisected the space as a roving spotlight made sure nobody defected.

Better yet, upon selecting which Korea to go with, a decision facilitated by uniform-and attitude-appropriate personnel, I was issued a passport with tasks to complete. Call me a communist, but I chose the NK and, at the risk of being hunted down as a traitor later, I can detail my time spent in the North.

I’ll let my issued Military Passport give you the gist of what was expected of me:

“Congratulations. You have been selected to serve the Northern Command, an honour granted to very few and refused by NONE.

Across this territory you will find operations. All participation, success or failure, will be stamped in this permit. Every stamp is yours to keep. Every victory, however, belongs to the North.”

Being proactive, I elbowed through a small sea of comrades to skip past the minigames, ascend centre stage and smash out a COD MW4 Campaign mission. Easy stamp, right there, folks. Side bonus: I even got some of my exploits replayed up on a screen the size of Kim Jong Il’s home cinema setup (he was quite the movie buff).

With early dominance secured, not only for myself, but for the glorious North entire, I descended back down into the other activities.

Honestly, there were some pretty nifty things to do. Operation Crossfire had me donning some NVGs and disappearing into a pitch-black shipping container to “acquire a target”. Once the traitor had been found and dispensed with, I moseyed over to Contraband Sweep and located anti-government items under threat of a time limit.

Glowing from my victory, I went and got a State Portrait, where I was informed that the North does not photograph happiness, only my resolve. I adjusted my smile accordingly.

The fun continued with me snooping around the space to find and secure Daily Truth propaganda documents. I also hunted down and confronted a (not-so) Covert Operative who was skulking about with a smug, democratic way about them that disgusted me to my very core. Upon confronting this Task Force 141 agitator, I seized their permit and uttered the codeword hidden within. His shame at discovery was palpable. The glorious North earned another stamp.

Before making my way to the Armoury to secure my booty, I infiltrated the South side to witness how life was for Capitalist hooligans. On account of the bile repeatedly rising up my throat while in their presence, I didn’t see everything these bourgeois delinquents got up to. I did, however, notice that they were earning their own stamps for defusing bombs with aid provided by troops in full kit.

What overwhelmingly was worth it, however, was attending this wonderful, MW4-themed side diversion. In case you haven’t read our review-in-progress yet, the general consensus (which includes me) is that the Campaign is quite a return to form for Infinity Ward.

Or, to put that more succinctly, the solo pillar of this sequel, and the pop-up event inspired by it, are stamp-worthy. And you can put that in your permit with confidence, comrade.

DMZ Early Access starts from 21 October for those who preorder - and the full game launches on 23 October in Australia .

articles.title: Valkyries lament their poor ball security as they fall to the Dream to even the WNBA Finals
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Angel Reese stole the ball from Kaila Charles and began dribbling when Tiffany Hayes tried to regain possession, fouled the Atlanta cent...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Angel Reese stole the ball from Kaila Charles and began dribbling when Tiffany Hayes tried to regain possession, fouled the Atlanta center and sent her to the floor. The Dream star repeatedly slapped her right hand on the court, finding yet another way to fire up her team.

Golden State's miscues kept coming, and Atlanta kept capitalizing — scoring 24 points off 19 turnovers to beat the Valkyries 79-65 in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals on Monday night and even the best-of-seven series at 1-all as it shifts to Atlanta.

"I think we were just a little too loose with the ball," Valkyries point guard Veronica Burton said. "Obviously that's what they're known for, and we're known for the opposite. It starts with me, I can't just be throwing the ball. It's one of the most important things is taking care of it and so I think just being organized, all being on the same page and then in fast break not getting too sped up, being decisive. I think we had a lot of times where we were hesitant or we weren't on the same page and that's where it led to turnovers."

Four of the five Golden State starters had two or more turnovers, with Kayla Thornton the only starter without one.

Rhyne Howard set a WNBA Finals single-game record with six steals and DeWanna Bonner chipped in four more off the bench. And Reese finished with 30 points and 16 rebounds.

Burton thought her team was outhustled by the determined Dream, who head home for Game 3 on Wednesday night. She committed three turnovers.

"You could tell that they ramped up their defense, so we've just got to stay focused, stay locked in," Golden State center Kiah Stokes said.

Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase credited the Dream for "their effort, their hustle, their fight," sprinting back on defense, getting their hands up and clogging the driving lanes.

"It's frustrating, that's been part of our identity. Because our identity is defense, we hang our hats on that," Nakase said. "The hustle is the turnovers because in order for you to get turnovers they have to kind of outhustle you to create the turnovers."

The Dream had just eight points off turnovers in their 68-64 Game 1 loss , then two days later returned to the defensive formula that got them this far. And that was crucial in tying up the series.

Nakase plans some conversations about sticking with a game plan and being organized on offense.

Burton will challenge herself to lead the way in taking better care of the ball.

"It starts with me. I've got to clean that up," she said, "and that's what we'll do."

articles.title: WNBA Finals winners and losers include Angel Reese's tenacity, Valkyries' starters
articles.summary: Angel Reese was unhappy with her Game 1 performance. She had a double-double as the Dream evened the WNBA Finals. Here are the winners and losers.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — Angel Reese was disappointed after the Atlanta Dream lost Game 1 of the WNBA Finals to the Golden State Valkyries and promised to pick it up.

The Dream All-Star posted a 30-point, 16-rebound double-double to fuel the 79-65 victory at Chase Center on Monday, Oct. 19. It was the first Finals victory across four series in franchise history."I was hungry, we wanted one and we felt like we let one slip away," Reese said.

Allisha Gray added 18 points and five rebounds for the Dream. Jordin Canada put up 13 points and 10 assists. Rhyne Howard broke the WNBA Finals record for most steals in a game with six takeaways.

The Valkyries were led by Gabby Williams and Tiffany Hayes, who both had 14 points. Veronica Burton added 11 points. Golden State shot 34% from the field and never led by more than six points.

The series heads to Atlanta for Games 3 and 4, beginning Wednesday, Oct. 21, at State Farm Arena.

"Atlanta, y'all better pull up and pop out," Reese said. "I'm looking forward to it."

Here are the winners and losers from Game 2.

WNBA Finals: Atlanta Dream and Valkyries clash for crown in Game 2

Angel Reese was held scoreless in the second half of Game 1 after a 14-point first half on Saturday. A disappointed Reese said she "let her team down" and vowed to leave it all on the floor in Game 2.

"I don't think they really did anything. Maybe that was just on me," Reese said after Game 1. "I wasn't aggressive enough with the ball and trying to get… to my spot. So I'm definitely going to do a better job of that next game."

Reese recorded a 30-point, 16-rebound double-double to secure the Dream's first WNBA Finals victory in franchise history, becoming the third player to score at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in a WNBA Finals game. Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones were the other two players to achieve the feat. Reese was the youngest to do it.

Funny enough, Reese said Stewart and Jones both spoke life into her after the Dream swept the New York Liberty in the semifinals: "The told me to go get it. They told me to keep going and pushing."

Reese's 30 points were a playoff career high and one point away from tying her WNBA career high. She shot 10-of-16 from the field, 1-of-1 from the 3-point line and 9-of-11 from the free-throw line. Reese rounded out her stat line with three assists, two blocks and one steal.

"We came and fought. I mean, Game 1 was tough for us, but we moved on and turned the page and got back to who we are," Reese said. "We watched film and saw the things that we messed up on. When I said that they didn't do anything to mess us up, it was literally just us and we can see that tonight and we going to carry that over in Atlanta."

Angel Reese earns WNBA Defensive Player of the Year. See her rise

Angel Reese and Allisha Gray both said the Dream got back to playing like themselves in Game 2, and that included being a ferocious transition team. Atlanta outscored Golden State 19-0 in fast-break points, which went a long way toward helping the Dream win the possession battle they lost in Game 1.

The Dream blew past their regular-season average of 11.9 fast-break points per game, which ranked second in the WNBA. They used their length to their advantage, jumped passing lanes and hounded Valkyries shooters in the corners. Atlanta scored 24 points off of 19 Golden State turnovers, often with Reese pushing the ball up the court and leading the break.

Atlanta played a more physical game than Golden State and it showed on the box score. Angel Reese dominated the glass, pulling down a total of 16 rebounds, including four on offense. As a team, the Dream narrowly outrebounded the Valkyries, 36-32, but it was their aggressiveness on both sides of the ball that really changed the game. They got up in the Valkyries' pockets, forcing Golden State into 19 forced turnovers. The Dream scored 24 points off the Valkyries' forced turnovers.

The Valkyries were completely discombobulated especially in the third quarter, where they were outscored 21-9.

A big part of Atlanta's recipe to success was their physicality and aggressiveness. In turn, it forced the official to make a call.

The Dream shot 86% from the free-throw line as a team, going 30-for-35. Atlanta had four players take at least six free-throw attempts in the game. Reese went 9-for-11. Allisha Gray only missed one free throw, shooting 7-for-8. Jordin Canda and DeWanna Bonner both shot 5-for-6 from the free-throw line.

They nearly doubled the Valkyries attempts. Golden State shot 16-of-19 on free-throws.

Gabby Williams has played hero for the Valkyries plenty of times this season, but on Monday she never hit the clutch-mode switch. Williams shot 3-of-15 from the field, including 1-of-6 on 3-pointers. It was by far her worst shooting performance this postseason.

Some of Williams' misses were the result of poor shot selection and forced looks late in the shot clock. Others were just unlucky, like the rare weakside wedgie on a 3-point attempt in the second quarter. But Williams also shanked a slew of open shots that she usually makes.

Williams was a perfect 7-for-7 at the foul line, which helped her score 14 points to lead the Valkyries along with reserve guard Tiffany Hayes, who also scored 14 points. Golden State's selling point is its depth, but the team might have leaned too much on Williams in Game 2 and kept feeding her in the hope that she'd eventually get hot. She couldn't deliver.

Gabby Williams is headed to the WNBA Finals. See her career in photos

It wasn't a good outing for the Valkyries' starters in Game 2 against the Dream. They were nearly outscored by Angel Reese, by herself. Reese dropped 30 points, Golden State's starters put up 32 points.

Gabby Williams led the Valkyries with 14 points, but she went 3-for-15 from the field. Cecilia Zandalasini went 1-for-8, connecting on a 3-pointer. Kayla Thornton wasn't aggressively looking for her shot only taking three attempts in the game. She made one.

Veronica Burton had a better shooting performance than Game 1. Burton shot 44% going 4-for-9 in their loss. Kiah Stokes did not take any shots in the 30 minutes she played.

The Valkyries turned the ball over 19 times in Monday's loss, a season-high. And the Dream capitalized on Golden State's mishaps, compiling 24 points off turnovers.

"We were just a little too loose with the ball. Obviously that's what they're known for and we're known for the opposite," Veronica Burton said. "We had a lot of times where we were hesitant or we weren't on the same page and that's where it led to turnovers."

Golden State head coach Natalie Nakase described the Valkyries' errors as "controllable." She said her team was outworked and outhustled in the matchup, which she called "frustrating."

"I need to have some conversations," Nakase said. "I need to listen within the next 48 hours to see how did I not deliver my message about our game plan, our fight, our physicality. ... Unfortunate and definitely going to ask questions."

Dream and Valkyries shooting output has been a struggle

The shooting in both games during the WNBA Finals have been poor. If people wanted offense, it is far and few in between at times. The grind is very real. Both teams shot under 35% in Game 2.

The reason? Both teams have elite defenses. Golden State had the top defense in the WNBA this season and Atlanta was third.

"What's (the Dream's) identity? Defense," Natalie Nakase said Monday. "We're a defensive-minded team. So we hang our hats on the defensive end. They played harder (tonight), and they were in the gaps better."

articles.title: Angel Reese, Sheryl Swoopes share special moment after Dream’s Game 2 win in WNBA Finals
articles.summary: It was a fitting image after the Atlanta Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries, 97-65, in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center on Monday. After the fin...
articles.body:
It was a fitting image after the Atlanta Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries, 97-65, in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center on Monday. After the final buzzer, Angel Reese ran toward Sheryl Swoopes at courtside and gave her a hug.

It looked like a passing of the torch, as if the WNBA legend told the third-year forward: "It's your time."

Reese had an evening against the Valkyries to tie the best-of-seven series at 1-1, tallying game-highs of 30 points and 16 rebounds. She also had three assists and two blocks and shot 10-of-16 from the field and 9-of-11 from the charity stripe.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

It was not clear what Reese and Swoopes talked about, but it was definitely encouraging for the 26-year-old star to have the support of an absolute legend.

Swoopes knows exactly what it takes to reach the mountaintop. She was a huge part of the dynastic run of the Houston Comets, capturing four straight titles from 1997 to 2000. The three-time MVP and seven-time All-WNBA was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2016.

Moreover, she was a three-time Defensive Player of the Year. Reese won the award for the first time this season.

Swoopes has always been a big fan of Reese, even defending the feisty forward during the peak of the national attention on her rivalry with Caitlin Clark in 2024.

After losing in Game 1, Reese vowed to be more aggressive on offense in Game 2. She stayed true to her promise, attacking the Valkyries from the outset . She had 15 points on 6-of-9 shooting from the field in the first half.

Game 3 will shift to State Farm Arena on Wednesday.

How Angel Reese, Dream played against Valkyries

articles.title: ‘Anti-American’ – Dream and Valkyries walking off court for national anthem again has fans fuming
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries made it a point to walk off the WNBA Finals court before Game 2 when the U. S.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries made it a point to walk off the WNBA Finals court before Game 2 when the U.S. national anthem was being performed.

After catching a lot of heat for walking off the court for the U.S. national anthem in Game 1, the Dream and Valkyries have done that once again in Game 2 at the Chase Center.

While legendary singer Alanis Morissette performed her rendition of 'The Star-Spangled Banner,' the players were caught on camera leaving seconds before the start of the anthem and returning the moment it ended.

Fans think the Dream and Valkyries are being 'anti-American'

If the reaction to the team's walking off for the national anthem was bad after Game 1, the situation seems to be worse after Game 2, as fans now know for sure that this is an intentional move by both teams rather than just a coincidence.

"The most anti-American thing you can do," said Craig Carton while fuming .

"Perhaps the league should move its operations to a country that better reflects its values," said an angry fan .

"The whole scene is ridiculous, but it's especially wild to me that not one player is like 'nope, I'm going to stand out here for my country,'" said one stunned fan who could not believe that no player on either team wants to respect the national anthem.

"You don't hate the WNBA enough!" said another angry fan .

"It's just bad. You can't spin it any other way," said one fan .

Supporters of both teams' decision are highlighting how it's a valid personal choice for players in a league that represents many communities who have been targeted or at odds with the current political regime.

It seems this will continue in Games 3 and 4 in Atlanta as well if the players are in agreement to continue with this form of silent protest. While they haven't come out and addressed their reasons, factors like the aggressive nationwide push to ban trans athletes from women's sports could be among the reasons.

articles.body:
Yandy Diaz blurted out "it all ends tomorrow" following the Game 5 win over the Cleveland Guardians . The Tampa Bay Rays designated hitter made good on that promise during the eighth inning. Now the Rays have earned their third American League title following the 7-3 home win.

Diaz sent Tropicana Field into a wild frenzy off this two-run home run rip that sealed the Game 6 victory.

Diaz blasted through a 75 miles per hour changeup and watched the ball sail 416 feet before scaling over the left field wall. He made good on his vow that he would help end the series.

From there, closer Bryan Baker forced two ground outs via his 83 mph changeup. Then he got Chase DeLauter out on a foul out that fell into the catcher's hands. And once again, Baker leaned into the changeup to send the Rays back to the World Series.

Tampa Bay even brought out former Rays stars Randy Arozarena and past pitcher Tyler Glasnow, the latter part of the last Rays World Series team of 2020. Glasnow took in the action after his Los Angeles Dodgers got swept by the Milwaukee Brewers.

Those ex-Rays stars watched new ALCS stars become birthed at "The Trop." Junior Caminero smashed a two-run home run that lifted the lead to 5-1 in the bottom of the seventh, which he ripped off his first swing. Chandler Simpson hit a personal milestone too , sprinting 3.78 seconds to first base following a bunt.

So now the Rays will face a franchise that also hasn't won a WS in their history. The Brewers are 0-1 lifetime on baseball's big stage. Milwaukee has tasted a baseball championship, though, which came in 1957 when the Braves represented the city.

articles.title: Dream’s Angel Reese reveals Liberty stars’ message that is fueling her in WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream stole a game on the road on Monday, beating the Golden State Valkyries, 79-65, in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center...
articles.body:
Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream stole a game on the road on Monday, beating the Golden State Valkyries, 79-65, in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center to tie the best-of-seven series at 1-1.

Reese led the charge with a double-double of 30 points and 16 rebounds, which were both game-highs, in 34 minutes. She added three assists and two blocks. She shot 10-of-16 from the field and 9-of-11 from the free-throw line.

The 26-year-0ld forward became only the third player in league history to post at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in the WNBA Finals , joining Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones of the New York Liberty. The beautiful coincidence was not lost on Reese.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"It's funny. They told me to go get it. They told me to keep going and push through in our last game in New York. So shout out to them, but I'm just doing whatever it takes to win," said Reese in the postgame interview.

The Dream swept the Liberty in the semifinals to advance to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. Reese averaged 20.6 points, 9.3 rebounds, 2.0 steals, and 1.7 blocks in the best-of-five series.

She touted their mentality in Game 2, acknowledging that they shot themselves in the foot in Game 1.

"This environment is tough to play in. Shout out to the fans. Shout out to my team, though. We came in. We fought. Game 1 was tough for us, but we moved on, turned the page, and got back to who we are," added the Defensive Player of the Year.

"Doing the little things, being intentional with every detail. We watched film and saw the things that we messed up."

Game 3 will move to State Farm Arena on Wednesday.

articles.title: Rays Win American League Pennant, Will Face Brewers in World Series
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays are heading to the World Series for the third time in their history. The American League's top seed defeated the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 i...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays are heading to the World Series for the third time in their history. The American League's top seed defeated the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 in Game 6 of the ALCS on Monday night, punching their ticket to the Fall Classic. The Rays won the pennant by turning the series around after falling behind 2-1, taking the last two games in Cleveland and then Game 6 back at Tropicana Field.

The Rays will now face the National League champion Milwaukee Brewers in the World Series starting on Friday. Both teams are vying for their first-ever World Series title.

Rays Win Pennant with Game 6 Victory over Guardians

Game 6 played out much like the previous two, with the Rays grabbing the lead and playing from ahead most of the way. Led by another strong outing from Freddy Peralta , the Rays' pitching staff held Cleveland off the scoreboard until the sixth inning. Peralta's third steady outing of the series (including two starts) would garner him ALCS MVP honors.

Meanwhile, Richie Palacios gave Tampa Bay another early lead. With two outs in the second inning, he poked a ball into right field that found the turf and turned into a clutch two-run double. Jonny DeLuca 's sacrifice fly one inning later stretched the lead to three, before Nathaniel Lowe answered back for Cleveland in the sixth with an RBI single to make it a 3-1 game.

The Rays delivered a pair of knockout punches in the later innings. In the bottom of the seventh, Junior Caminero hit a two-run home run off the left-field foul pole to give Tampa Bay a 5-1 lead. Cleveland made things interesting in the eighth as Rays reliever Ian Seymour faltered, issuing a walk and a hit-by-pitch with the bases loaded to make it a 5-3 game. However, in the bottom of the frame, Yandy Díaz hit another two-run blast to restore the four-run lead and put the game away.

It's worth noting that Díaz and Caminero both started their professional careers in Cleveland's minor league system. Díaz even played parts of two seasons for the then-Indians (2017-2018) before getting traded to the Rays. It's a gut punch for Guardians fans to see two of their former prospects help finish off their team in October.

While the Guardians briefly held the upper hand in this ALCS, the better team ultimately won out. The well-rounded Rays got timely hitting in the last three games and made big plays when they needed to. Their strong pitching, especially from Peralta and breakout closer Bryan Baker, helped to quash the Guardians' offense as the series turned.

The Rays will now shift their focus to the Brewers, who had the best record in MLB this year, and are fresh off a sweep of the two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers. This Fall Classic will be a clash of the titans, with the two top seeds in each league facing off for the title. Milwaukee will likely be favored in the series and will have home-field advantage, but don't sleep on a very deep Rays team that can hold their own against any opponent. No matter who emerges on top, we will see history this October with one team winning it all for the first time .

articles.title: Why did Dream win Game 2 vs. Valkyries? Allisha Gray’s 2-word answer is epic
articles.summary: Allisha Gray needed just two words to explain how the Atlanta Dream bounced back in the 2026 WNBA Finals: “Angel Reese.” The Dream forward delivered a domina...
articles.body:
Allisha Gray needed just two words to explain how the Atlanta Dream bounced back in the 2026 WNBA Finals: "Angel Reese." The Dream forward delivered a dominant 30-point, 16-rebound performance to power Atlanta past the Golden State Valkyries, 79-65 , in Game 2 at Chase Center. The win evened the championship series at one game apiece. After struggling to find its footing in the opener, Atlanta flipped the script behind Reese's relentless interior presence . That overwhelmed Golden State's defense and created opportunities for the rest of the lineup.

Gray added 18 points, while Rhyne Howard made Finals history with six steals. That helped the Dream control the game on both ends. Reese, though, was the undisputed centerpiece. She imposed her will from the opening tip and gave Atlanta the physical edge it needed to secure the franchise's first WNBA Finals victory. When asked what made the difference after the final buzzer, Gray pointed directly to her teammate with the succinct response that said it all. Reese's performance gave the Dream renewed belief as the series shifts to Georgia.

Atlanta's championship push has been building all season. The Dream tied a franchise record with 30 regular-season wins to earn the No. 3 seed. They then swept the Washington Mystics and New York Liberty to reach the Finals undefeated in the postseason. Their Game 1 loss to Golden State was the first real setback of their playoff run. However, Game 2 showed how quickly they can respond when Reese anchors the offense and defense. Gray's scoring and Howard's disruptive defense further demonstrated the depth behind Atlanta's star forward. With the series now tied 1-1 and the next games moving to Atlanta, the Dream have a chance to turn Reese's breakthrough Finals performance into a championship-defining run.

articles.title: Disney Will Air a Real-Time, Animated Version of the 2027 Super Bowl Set in the Star Wars Universe
articles.summary: The dark side of the Force is a pathway to many abilities some consider to be unnatural.
articles.body:
Disney and the NFL have confirmed a real-time, animated “alternate telecast” of Super Bowl LXI, set in the Star Wars galaxy, will stream live on Disney+ and the ESPN App (and air on Disney Channel and Disney XD) on February 14, 2027. According to the announcement, this animated version of the next Super Bowl will feature characters from “across the Lucasfilm franchise”, and it’s specifically noted Anthony Daniels would be returning to voice C-3PO.

Dubbed “Star Wars Funday Football”, the company notes this production will give “fans of all ages a new way to experience ESPN’s first-ever Super Bowl production.”

However, while Star Wars Funday Football will be the first animated alternate broadcast of a Super Bowl, it will otherwise be the fourth of its kind from ESPN, Disney, and the NFL (following the Sports Emmy Award-winning Toy Story Funday Football in 2023, The Simpsons Funday Football in 2024, and Monsters Funday Football in 2025).

The broadcasts are made possible via “data visualization technology” from Sony’s Beyond Sports, which converts real-time player tracking data into animation in real-time. If you haven’t seen it in action, it converts the spectacle of real human skill and athleticism into what looks like a licensed mobile game, only you can’t affect the outcome, and it goes for three hours.

With 2027 marking the 50th anniversary of Star Wars, Star Wars Funday Football will air just five days before a newly restored version of the original 1977 Star Wars returns to cinemas on February 19, 2027.

articles.title: Liverpool day trips hit as ferry times change
articles.summary: Some November sailings will now return at an earlier time during the day.
articles.body:
Passengers who had booked day trips to Liverpool next month will have to change their plans now the Isle of Man Steam Packet Company brought forward four weekend return sailings.

The Liverpool to Isle of Man crossings on 7, 14, 21 and 28 November will now depart at 13:30 GMT instead of 19:00.

The company said the change was due to tidal and operational issues.

The revised timetable comes as the Ben-my-Chree continues to cover the main Heysham route while the flagship Manxman undergoes repairs.

Affected passengers will be contacted by the Steam Packet, with full refunds available where no suitable alternative sailing can be found.

Passengers can instead transfer to the 01:45 GMT sailing from Heysham, with coaches provided for foot passengers travelling from Liverpool. Coach travel must be booked at the same time as the amended sailing.

The Manxman has been out of service since wear was discovered on its propulsion shafts during routine dry docking in July.

articles.title: There's Real Force Behind These Star Wars Battlefront 3 Rumors
articles.summary: Talk of Star Wars Battlefront 3 has ramped up this week, with a number of studios reportedly in with a chance of developing the shooter sequel.
articles.body:
Talk of Star Wars Battlefront 3 has ramped up this week, with a number of studios reportedly in with a chance of developing the shooter sequel.

The rumor kicked off when Giant Bomb’s Jeff Grubb read out a snippet from Electronic Gaming Monthly’s revived Quarterman column, which claimed Disney has “big plans” for the Star Wars Battlefront series. According to EGM, Lucasfilm is looking for a development partner for Battlefront 3, and two studios are “circling” the project: DICE, developer of Battlefield and Battlefront, and Bungie, developer of Halo, Destiny, and Marathon.

The potential for a Battlefront 3 is hugely exciting for fans of the series, of course, and if it does end up green lit, DICE would be the obvious course to develop it, although how the game would fit with the ongoing work on the Battlefield series remains to be seen.

Bungie, though, would be a huge surprise as developer of Battlefront 3. The Sony-owned studio is working to turn around struggling extraction shooter Marathon, and only last month Bungie said more Destiny is coming , months after ending support for Destiny 2. It feels unlikely that Bungie would have the scope to make a fully fleshed out Battlefront 3, at least not any time soon. Would parent company Sony even be receptive to such an idea? Would Bungie?

Plot twist! Joe Brammer, boss of Wardogs developer Bulkhead, just… tweeted it out . But rather than Bungie, it’s Titanfall, Apex Legends, and Star Wars Jedi developer Respawn that’s working with DICE on Battlefront 3, according to Brammer. "DICE and from what I’ve heard Respawn are working on Battlefront 3," he said on X / Twitter. "Not sure what that means for Battlefield."

What’s actually going on here? Well, it doesn’t sound like Battlefront 3 is in production yet, if Lucasfilm is on the hunt for development partners. But it’s entirely plausible that DICE and Respawn have done pre-production work, fleshing out what the game will be and how it will work, while looking for studios to help build it.

And before we get our hopes up, it’s worth remembering that Battlefront fans have been here before. TimeSplitters developer Free Radical Design has a Battlefront 3 game that was pretty much done before it fell by the wayside around 2008. Assets and even builds of the game have leaked online ever since.

EA eventually had DICE pick up the mantle and reboot the series with the hugely popular Star Wars Battlefront in 2015. But its sequel, 2017’s Battlefront 2, suffered a disastrous launch fueled by a backlash to loot boxes . DICE spent years righting the ship, to the point now where Battlefront 2 is held in pretty high regard .

If DICE is working on Battlefront 3 in some capacity, it’ll do so without much of the original development team, which scattered to various studios in Sweden and abroad in the wake of Battlefront 2’s release. Some of the developers went to Embark, developer of The Finals and Arc Raiders. Indeed, I’ve already seen some suggest Embark as the perfect fit for a Battlefront 3.

Star Wars video games are in a positive moment, with the positive reception to Bit Reactor’s strategy game Zero Company and Fuse Games’ Galactic Racer sparking excitement over what might come next from the franchise. Lucasfilm Games vice president Douglas Reilly recently told The Game Business that “huge triple-A games like Battlefront are always going to be an essential part of the strategy,” but smaller-scale games in different genres are also in the works.

"Good ideas can come from a lot of different places. You don’t have to necessarily be a top five publisher to make a great Star Wars game,” he continued. “There are some hurdles. We have a high quality bar, and that means typically we work with more experienced teams than ones with no track record. But we’re exploring all kinds of things, large and small, with partners that are going to surprise folks."

articles.title: Xbox 'Business Strategist' Claims Video Game Industry Is 'Pretending to Not Use AI,' Deletes Twitter Account After Deluge of Replies
articles.summary: An Xbox staff member went viral this week for taking to social media to tell "the truth that nobody wants you to know": that the video game industry is "pretending" to not use AI.
articles.body:
An Xbox staff member went viral this week for taking to social media to tell "the truth that nobody wants you to know": that the video game industry is "pretending" to not use AI.

Xbox Business Strategist, Brandon Stirrup, tweeted to say he'd used AI to create a "little bad game" after just three hours of work. He then used that as a springboard to talk about AI in gaming, and how the technology is more widely used than the industry lets on.

In his posts, which have been preserved on Reddit, Stirrup insisted that "gaming is the only industry pretending not to use AI," and, "If you're a game developer refusing to believe that AI has a place in your future, you should not be in the business of being a business."

Stirrup added: "Look if I'm fired tomorrow it will be because I told you the truth that nobody wants you to know. You can make a game with a simple prompt and yes you can make custom, tailored games. Everything you want in a game is right there for the taking, for better or worse.

"I'm happy to take the hit if it means hundreds at Xbox can stop pretending that they're not using AI. It's time to accept and move forward."

"I love Xbox and Microsoft and I have spent 10+ years proving this," he added. "My goal is to get this over with so we can move on as a company, despite the fact that some will persecute me for this: we use AI, just as all companies do in 2026."

The comments sparked a flood of responses on social media, which a source at Xbox indicated led to Stirrup disabling his X / Twitter account.

AI is the hottest topic in the industry. Fortnite developer Epic Games has already declared that code for its upcoming Star Wars shooter is going to be entirely written by AI, with the game director even declaring "no handwritten code" for the game. Epic boss Tim Sweeney has spent much of the last week trumpeting AI on social media, even as some hit out at the company's plans and its "vibe-coded" Epic Games launcher .

Capcom also had a presentation recently where it presented 'REX' as a way to help the RE engine continue to mature, using, you guessed it, AI. However, the Resident Evil developer subsequently clarified that it would just be integrating AI tools to boost "the efficiency and productivity of the game development process," rather than using generative AI to create assets and code wholesale.

AI is also being increasingly used for decompilation and modding. There's been an entire wave of AI-assisted mashup mods on X / Twitter that continues to gain traction. Plus, AI has become such a big part of the decomp scene that it's forced at least one community focused on manual decompilation to go offline . Microsoft has responded to this wave of AI in the modding community by launching Xbox Labs , which aims to do a lot of the same things that the community is already doing, including porting games to browsers.

Perhaps more impactful — or damaging, if you're in the business of selling video game consoles — is the role of AI in jailbreaking hardware. Sony is currently facing the possibility of a PS5 jailbreak on the eve of the launch of GTA 6, which could, theoretically at least, open the door to people making Rockstar's game available on PC. Rockstar parent company Take-Two would likely take a dim view of the PS5's encryption if that were to happen.

As for Stirrup's claims, the only aspect of AI that game developers have meaningfully distanced themselves from by large is art and asset generation. As AI tools continue to mature, they're only going to be used in games more often. Heck, even Epic's Unreal Engine, which is used in every other game these days, has generative AI tools built into the UI . So, if this is the state of AI in gaming when developers are "pretending" to not use it, what will it look like when these companies stop "pretending?"

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Techland CEO Addresses Fans as Dying Light: The Beast Support Comes to an End
articles.summary: Techland’s founder and CEO, Paweł Marchewka, recently hosted a Discord AMA with fans of the company’s parkour-fueled zombie series, during which he announced the end of support for Dying Light: The Beast.
articles.body:
Techland’s founder and CEO, Paweł Marchewka, recently hosted a Discord AMA with fans of the company’s parkour-fueled zombie series, during which he announced the end of support for Dying Light: The Beast . The game landed last year as a standalone release, despite its original positioning as an expansion for Dying Light 2.

The Beast recently got the Restored Land update , which allowed players to clear out the zombies across the map and bring civilization back to the world. But now support is ending for The Beast, which Techland never planned as a game the company would support long term.

Dying Light: The Beast is a complete game, and that’s how players should approach it — much like Dying Light 1 is today,” Marchewka said, via Insider Gaming . “We’re not planning substantial new content for it.”

Marchewka went on to say that The Beast was planned as a “complete, self-contained game from the start.” The company never made a commitment to it, but still put out substantial free updates over the past year, including Restored Land, new weapons, and more.

“The five-year support model hasn’t worked as well for us as we hoped,” Marchewka continued. “We’re an AAA studio. With each new game, we want to deliver an unforgettable experience and push the boundaries of what games can do.”

The CEO went on to explain how supporting multiple games can impact development on the studio’s next release. “Supporting existing games for years with smaller teams can seriously disrupt work on new projects,” he said.

“At the same time, players expect frequent, substantial, high-quality updates — sometimes several times a month, and usually for free. With limited resources, we can end up disrupting production and still disappointing players.”

The team will continue to support Dying Light 2, which still has a larger team working on updates than Dying Light ever had. Techland’s next game was supposed to be its fantasy RPG project , but that was canceled last year.

The Xbox One and PS4 versions of The Beast were also canceled earlier this year. What Techland is working on next remains a mystery for now.

articles.title: Angel Reese proves why she’s the Dream’s ultimate giver in confidence, energy and buckets
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO — What Angel Reese wants, she usually gets. She wills the world she wants into existence because she seems genuinely unaware that any other out...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — What Angel Reese wants, she usually gets. She wills the world she wants into existence because she seems genuinely unaware that any other outcome is possible. It's either a tremendous superpower or a kind of nefarious spell conjured by the villain in the story, depending on your view of her — which, by the way, she could not care less about.

How strange that the Atlanta Dream forgot about this to start the WNBA Finals. How predictable that Reese would have enough of that at some point. Because here she was Monday, backpedaling in the third quarter of Game 2, waving her arms, begging her coaches to get her the ball if her teammates couldn't or wouldn't. The best player on the floor for the Dream somehow slipped everyone's minds — again.

"I'm not going to tell you exactly what I said," Reese noted after a 79-65 win over the Golden State Valkyries that rewrote records and reset this championship round at one game apiece. But then again, she didn't have to. Everyone on her side got the idea. Everyone in the building got the idea. Everyone got an earful, then got an eyeful of maybe the strongest force of personality in the league.

When attempting to run through a wall, why not follow the person who refuses to believe it's there in the first place?

"Going in the locker room (before the game), the first person I made eye contact with was Angel," Dream coach Karl Smesko said. "And I'm like, 'Oh, I like this look.'"

The look is the point. The 30 points and the 16 rebounds are not beside the point, of course, not when Reese became the youngest of the six players ever to post those numbers in a WNBA playoff game. Nor is the franchise's first finals win, arriving a few months after she did . These are milestones.

But they stand upon an almost comically large mountain of belief.

When Angel Reese is on your side, she is the ultimate confidence-giver. She runs on belief and defiance and aggression, and she assumes her teammates take the same octane as she does. She pours it into their tanks, too. She brings everybody along on the ride.

So starting this series on the road, in the Ballhalla cauldron, was most people's idea of a problem for Atlanta. It might be Reese's idea of fresh air.

And the reason everyone wondered where she went in the second half of Game 1, taking just two shots from the floor, was due to the fact that she was everywhere in the first half. Nobody on the Dream approached the challenge of the Valkyries defense more insistently. Just a little more commitment to the bit, for a little longer, and the results might have been different.

Reese flogged herself in the hours after Saturday's series-opening loss — "I think I let the team down, and that was on me," she said. "I wasn't aggressive enough" — but the reality of her game at age 24 is that she can't create offense entirely by herself, at least not all the time. The right plan and regular passing of the ball are required. In Game 2, Smesko schemed Reese into the best possible spots to get her downhill, and her teammates played through her. When they didn't, they were notified that they should start doing so again, immediately.

"At one point, she was like, 'I need the ball! I need the ball!'" Dream point guard Jordin Canada said. "We gave her the ball. And she went to work."

Basically by herself, Reese upset the equilibrium of the series. She made 10 of her 16 shot attempts. The rest of the athletes who competed Monday went 32-of-107 from the field.

But you can also draw a line between her attitude and the discombobulation of the Valkyries. Reese talked about playing "hungry" and "pissed." Golden State talked about taking too many punches without punching back. It all meant the same thing, and it was effectively all about the same person.

"You can just see she wants it really bad," Canada said. "We feed off her energy. She set the tone, for sure. And it just trickled down through the whole team."

She would know. She would know how this works. Canada spent a portion of the postgame news conference discussing how bummed she was about herself, and in particular her shooting. A few minutes later, as the Dream contingent walked back to the locker room, Reese addressed Canada with a smile.

"You were good!" she told her point guard. "You did a lot of great things for us!"

Until a star delivers like this in a moment like this, the audience is free to question whether they can. Reese's answer in Game 2 is less a rejoinder than a threat. She can fill a box score, and while doing so, she can make her group believe like her. Whatever unease the Dream might've felt about their championship chops after Game 1 is gone. It's replaced by a sense that anything goes from here.

After Monday's win, every Atlanta player had long since disappeared into the visitors locker room when Reese headed up the ramp after postgame television interview duties. When she made that same walk after the series opener, she didn't feel like herself. She wanted to be sure she left the floor after Game 2 reassured of who she was.

And this was more like it. This looked like what she wants.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Gets Surprise Official New Update Announcement From CD Projekt
articles.summary: CD Projekt has announced a surprise update to Cyberpunk 2077, due out this week.
articles.body:
CD Projekt has announced a surprise update to Cyberpunk 2077, due out this week.

The Cyberpunk 2077 Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) launches Thursday, October 22, and while CD Projekt kept the details quiet, it has confirmed it will feature content "inspired" by the anime. Edgerunners 2 hits Netflix today, so this update is well-timed to capitalize on heightened interest in all things Cyberpunk 2077.

But what, exactly, is in the update itself? CD Projekt took to social media to confirm that Cyberpunk 2077 will get "new items and features," which includes the content inspired by Edgerunners 2."

"Update 2.5 will be dropping on October 22, 2026, marking yet another opportunity to dive back into Night City or experience it for the very first time," the developer continued.

What does new "features" mean? Fans are hoping for more than minor Edgerunners cosmetics. Rather, they’re hoping for substantial DLC that includes new content. Maybe even a new official, CD Projekt-made quest.

“So f***ing hyped about what we cooked for you,” teased Paweł Sasko , associate game director on the in-development Cyberpunk 2. Perhaps fans should get their hopes up, then.

Every CD Projekt Red Game In Development

More details about the Edgerunners 2 Update will be revealed on October 21, 2026, during a special episode of REDstreams, CD Projekt said. Patch notes are scheduled for publication on the same day. The free update itself launches across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X and S, with the Nintendo Switch 2 release to "follow shortly."

Cyberpunk 2077 fans have been calling on CD Projekt to release meaningful DLC for some time now . Some even hold out hope for an expansion for the near six-year-old game, especially in light of the announcement of the Songs of the Past expansion for the 11-year-old The Witcher 3.

In May, CD Projekt insisted it had “no plans” for further Cyberpunk 2077 DLCs or expansions , disappointing fans. The comment suggested that fans would have to wait for Cyberpunk 2 for more from CD Projekt’s much-loved dystopian universe. And the wait looks like it's going to be significant; Cyberpunk 2 is further behind The Witcher 4, and CD Projekt co-CEO Michał Nowakowski has suggested Cyberpunk 2 won’t be out until at least 2030.

But this news of a 2.5 update for Cyberpunk 2077 runs counter somewhat to CD Projekt's statement in May, and has already got fans either dusting off their download, or redownloading the game in anticipation of what's to come.

In July, CD Projekt confirmed that Cyberpunk 2077 had sold an incredible 40 million copies since its December 2020 launch, up 5 million from November 2025. It's received one expansion so far, 2023's Phantom Liberty starring Idris Elba.

While you wait to find out what's in this new Cyberpunk 2077 update, check out IGN's review of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 .

articles.title: Kratos Would Have Had a Different Name Were It Not for Relentless Domino's Pizza Jokes, God of War Creator Reveals
articles.summary: God of War's Kratos almost went by a different name, but developers at Santa Monica Studio made too many Domino's pizza jokes.
articles.body:
God of War's Kratos almost went by a different name, but developers at Santa Monica Studio made too many Domino's pizza jokes. David Jaffe, the director of the original God of War trilogy, recently put out a video explaining the deep dish issue.

Originally, Kratos was called “Dominus,” which Jaffe liked because it made him sound dominant and strong. Unfortunately, it also made him sound like a chain of pizza restaurants.

“The people on the team started making Domino’s Pizza jokes,” Jaffe said . “Every single time someone said Dominus, someone inevitably would yell out, ‘30 minutes or free,’ or, ‘Get the door, it’s Dominus.’

“After about the 50th time, the writing was on the wall. Dominus was dead and we needed a new name for our hero.”

Someone at the studio printed out a big list of Ancient Greek baby names and Jaffe went through with a yellow highlighter marking the best ones. “The names that I highlighted were not great,” he said, pointing at Julius, Parthenius, and Maksym as examples.

“Nothing felt just right. Eventually, our marketing lead, Susan Panico, was the one who came up with the name Kratos. She pitched it and we loved it, and it stuck.”

Jaffe found the list of highlighted baby names among his old design documents last year. On the sheet, hidden among the names, unhighlighted, there it was: Kratos.

“We had Sony’s biggest franchise hero in our hands the entire time and we didn’t even know it,” he said. “Which I guess goes to show you how much of success in games is just luck, timing, and, in this case, marketing.”

Jaffe has previously talked about Dominus and the creation of Kratos, but he’s never gone into this much detail about the process. He previously just said that marketing didn’t like Dominus, but the pizza stuff is certainly a new development.

God of War's first release was the 2005 PS2 game of the same name. It was a big hit, spawning a franchise that has seen significant success over the past 20 years. The next game in the series, God of War: Laufey, is due out on PS5 in February 2027. Santa Monica Studio head of creative Cory Barlog has confirmed that an untitled new God of War game with Kratos back as the protagonist is also in development .

articles.title: Tecno Pova 8 Pro 5G review: Stylish looks, capable performance
articles.summary: Rating: 3.5/5 Smartphones today are expected to do much more than handle calls and messages.
articles.body: Rating: 3.5/5Smartphones today are expected to do much more than handle calls and messages. We use them to work, watch videos, play games, take photographs and navigate unfamiliar places, often for hours at a stretch. As brands add AI tools and decorative design elements, the basics still matter: a display that stays visible outdoors, dependable battery life, comfortable handling, and software that doesn't get in the way.The Tecno Pova 8 Pro 5G promises to balance these everyday requirements with gaming-focused hardware and a distinctive design. Priced at Rs 49,999, the smartphone features a MediaTek Dimensity 7400 Ultimate 5G processor, a dedicated P1 graphics chip, a 6.78-inch 1.5K AMOLED display with a 144Hz refresh rate and a 6,500mAh battery.It also comes with a 50MP primary camera with optical image stabilisation, a 13MP front camera, and a rear notification system called Alive Matrix. We tested the Tecno Pova 8 Pro 5G in the Tundra Green colour option, with the 8GB RAM and 256GB storage variant. After spending time with the phone, here’s what we think about the Tecno Pova 8 Pro 5G:DesignThe phone's design stands out from the usual glass-and-metal slabs in this segment. The rear panel has a textured finish around the edges, angular patterns across the back and a prominent camera module that follows the brand’s signature triangular design language. The green finish looks good in hand, and the overall build gives the phone a premium feel.The camera module also houses the Alive Matrix Display, a dot-matrix panel that can show visual effects and information. Tecno presents it as more than a decorative element, with features such as notifications, battery status, timers and caller identification. However, in our experience, it felt more like a design gimmick than a feature we'd use regularly. The battery also drains faster when it's kept enabled.Despite its distinctive rear design, the Pova 8 Pro 5G remains comfortable to hold. Its proportions make it manageable for one-handed use, and the textured back adds to its visual appeal.All physical buttons, including the power button, volume rockers and Action button, are located on the right side. We could customise the Action button to perform different functions, such as triggering the camera shutter or turning on the flashlight.DisplayThe display is one of the phone's stronger aspects. The Pova 8 Pro 5G features a 6.78-inch 1.5K AMOLED panel with a refresh rate of up to 144Hz. In everyday use, scrolling feels smooth, whether we are moving through social media feeds, browsing websites, or switching between apps.Outdoor visibility is another positive. We could see almost everything on the screen even under direct sunlight, making it easier to read messages, check navigation, and use apps outdoors without constantly searching for shade. This is particularly useful when traveling or using the phone during the day.The AMOLED panel also makes watching movies and series a pleasant experience. While watching titles such as The Dark Knight, Avengers: Endgame, and Game of Thrones, the display's contrast helped darker scenes retain their depth, while the colours added to the visual appeal of action sequences and detailed environments.The 1.5K resolution also made the content look sharp, and the large screen offered an immersive viewing experience. The high refresh rate is more noticeable while navigating the interface and gaming than when watching most films and series, which are typically presented at lower frame rates.Tecno claims peak brightness of up to 4,500 nits and high brightness mode of up to 1,600 nits. These are different brightness measurements, and actual visibility depends on the content displayed, ambient light and operating conditions. Our experience in direct sunlight was positive, but we would not treat the advertised peak figure as a brightness level sustained across the entire display.The phone also supports high-frequency PWM dimming to reduce visible flicker at lower brightness levels. Overall, the display is a strong point, combining smooth scrolling with good outdoor visibility.Performance and softwareThe Tecno Pova 8 Pro 5G runs on the MediaTek Dimensity 7400 Ultimate chipset, paired with a dedicated P1 graphics chip. Tecno has also included a 5,000mm² vapour chamber cooling system to manage heat during demanding tasks.In our experience, the phone offered capable gaming performance. We played high-graphics titles like BGMI and Real Cricket, along with a few casual games. We didn’t notice any lag or stutter while playing any of the titles. However, the phone got slightly warm during extended gaming sessions. It also warmed slightly in direct sunlight or while charging at full power. The heating was noticeable but didn't affect the device's overall usability.The software experience is overall smooth. The phone runs HiOS 16, which offers several customization options and productivity tools. We also came across a few minor UI bugs during regular use. However, they weren't significant enough to affect every interaction, and many users may not notice them in everyday use. Still, there is room to improve the software polish.The AI features were also helpful. Tools such as Ask Ella, AI Writing and AI Mind Hub are designed to assist with tasks including summarising web pages, generating text, and solving problems. All the tools did a decent job in our testing.CameraThe Tecno Pova 8 Pro 5G features a 50MP Sony LYTIA 700C primary camera with optical image stabilisation, an 8MP ultra-wide camera and a 13MP front camera. The primary sensor is designed to capture detailed images, while optical stabilisation helps reduce blur caused by movement.In our experience, the rear camera delivered decent results. It suits everyday photography and capturing memories for social media. Tecno also offers AI-powered editing tools for tasks such as removing reflections, shadows and lens flare, along with features like AI Auto Zoom and FlashSnap. AI processing helped in some situations, and the results were mostly consistent. Here are some camera samples:The 13MP front camera also offered a decent experience. The selfies were beautiful and looked social media-ready.Battery and chargingBattery life is one of the Pova 8 Pro 5G's more dependable aspects. The phone packs a 6,500mAh battery, and in our regular usage, it comfortably lasted around a day and a half. This included everyday activities such as browsing, messaging, watching videos and using apps. That kind of endurance reduces the need to look for a charger every evening.Charging is another area where the phone performs reasonably well. Tecno advertises 45W charging, and we found the phone could charge fully in about an hour at full-power settings. This makes topping up the large battery more convenient than the capacity alone might suggest. The phone supports three charging speeds. However, it gets slightly warm when charging at the highest speed.Connectivity and audioConnectivity on the Tecno Pova 8 Pro 5G was good enough for everyday use. We didn't find any major issues with the basic connectivity experience, and the phone meets the usual requirements of a modern 5G smartphone.The device also includes stereo speakers with Dolby Atmos support. The audio quality is adequate for watching videos, following dialogue, and playing games, and it stands out as a defining feature. The large display and speakers make the phone well-suited for casual video consumption.VerdictThe Tecno Pova 8 Pro 5G gets most of the fundamentals right. Its display is smooth and remains visible in direct sunlight, the phone feels premium and comfortable to hold, and the 6,500mAh battery delivers around a day and a half of normal use. Gaming performance is decent, and the 45W charging system can refill the battery in an hourThe cameras and the AI features are decent. The rear Alive Matrix lighting system is visually distinctive and offers some practical value, and HiOS 16 feels smooth and polished.Starting at Rs 49,999, the Pova 8 Pro 5G is a solid option for buyers who want a good display, smooth performance, and dependable battery life.You use AI every day. articles.title: Angel Reese delivers historic WNBA Finals response after quiet Game 1 finish
articles.summary: The Dream star turned frustration into a 30-point, 16-rebound performance that changed the championship series.
articles.body:
Angel Reese spent the two days between WNBA Finals games with something to prove. She had scored 14 points in Atlanta's Game 1 loss to Golden State, but none came after halftime. When the Dream returned to Chase Center on Monday night, Reese made sure the second half would tell a different story.

Reese scored 30 points and grabbed 16 rebounds in Atlanta's 79-65 victory over the Valkyries, evening the best-of-seven series at one game apiece. She shot 10-for-16 from the field, added three assists and two blocks, and delivered the kind of performance that changes how an opponent must prepare for the next game.

The numbers were historic. Reese became just the third player to record at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in a WNBA Finals game, joining Jonquel Jones in 2019 and Breanna Stewart in 2020. It was not simply a big scoring night. It was an emphatic response to the way Golden State had contained her late in the opener.

Atlanta needed every part of that response. The Dream entered Monday still seeking the franchise's first Finals victory after going winless across three previous championship-series appearances. Their breakthrough came against a Valkyries team that had won Game 1, 68-64, and carried the energy of a sold-out home crowd.

Reese was not alone. Allisha Gray scored 18 points, Jordin Canada supplied 13 points and 10 assists, and Rhyne Howard set a Finals record with six steals. Atlanta held Golden State to nine points in the third quarter, taking control after a competitive first half.

The series moves to Atlanta for Game 3 on Wednesday, with the next two contests scheduled for State Farm Arena rather than the Dream's smaller regular home. The larger building provides a bigger stage for a team that has suddenly found its first Finals win.

Golden State still has plenty of reasons to believe it can respond. Gabby Williams scored 26 points in Game 1, and the Valkyries earned their Finals opportunity with a strong postseason run. But they now must answer a different question: how to defend a version of Reese that attacks rather than waits for the game to come to her.

Monday did not decide the championship. It did make one thing clear. Atlanta's best player is prepared to make this a much longer series.
